metadata.case_name: CHAN KWOK PING v. HOP YICK ENGINEERING CO. AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: painter and plasterer at construction sites
plaintiff.occupation_after: painting worker in interior decoration work in domestic and office premises

source: on 9th November 1990 the Plaintiff was found to have a large corneal ulcer.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of eye or orbit

source: The ulcer was subsequently healed resulting information of a vascularised corneal scar.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of eye or orbit

injuries.description: visual impairment of right eye (visual acuity 3/60)
source: The visual acuity of the right eye is 3/60.
Visual acuity test revealed vision right eye 3/60, left eye 6/6 unaided, with no improvement on pinhole or spectacles.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of eye or orbit, unspecified

source: the Plaintiff has been suffering from right eye recurrent cornea epithelial erosion, which is a well known complication after any kinds of cornea injury.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of conjunctiva or corneal abrasion without mention of foreign body

source: band keratopathy developed gradually on the diseased cornea.
The corneal epithelium shows irregularity with patches of calcification lying horizontally, indicating presence of band keratopathy.
Vascularized pannus was present, especially over the superior part of the cornea and limbus.

manifestations.description: Reduced vision in right eye (vision 3/60) obscuring the visual axis
Right eye pain and recurrent episodes where he "could not see with his right eye"; pain described as "like being bitten by ants" occurring around 4 p.m. each day
Vascularized pannus and corneal opacity affecting the cornea and visual axis
Band keratopathy (patches of calcification and corneal epithelial irregularity)

treatments_received: immediate eye irrigation: washed it with water for 15 minutes
medical examination and follow-up by ophthalmologists
treatments_future: cornea transplant (Hospital Authority of Ophthalmic Unit had suggested the Plaintiff to undergo a cornea transplant, but he was reluctant to have the operation)

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities
Unable to work on construction sites; reduced ability to perform quality painting work and reduced working days per month

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Wan Tak v. Suen Yiu Pan trading as Chiu Kee Sawmill
